title: Sunk Cost Fallacy
coreMove: Break the false inference inside sunk cost, then decide from current evidence instead of the tempting story.
sourcePressure: The source sidecar and official source notes frame Sunk Cost Fallacy as a specific decision error around sunk cost, non-refundable, Concorde fallacy. Traceable support includes The Psychology of Sunk Cost.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating Sunk Cost Fallacy as generic advice to be smarter, instead of forcing this exact move: break the false inference inside sunk cost, then decide from current evidence instead of the tempting story.

sourceAnchors.name: The Psychology of Sunk Cost
sourceAnchors.detail: The classic research on the sunk cost fallacy is: H. R. Arkes and C. Blumer, ' The Psychology of Sunk Cost ' , Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes (1985, 35), 124 - 140. In this research, Arkes and Blumer asked subjects to imagine that they had purchased tickets
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The Psychology of Sunk Cost can appear as a factual pressure point: the reader sees sunk cost fallacy through evidence, not a decorative citation.

hook: Do not open with a definition of Sunk Cost Fallacy.
Do not use a generic panic-at-a-meeting opener.
counterintuition: Avoid the reusable shape where the obvious answer is wrong and the opposite is true.
Do not make Sunk Cost Fallacy sound like ordinary carelessness.
examples: No coffee mug, classroom whiteboard, bus depot, radiator, bike helmet, or narrow kitchen shell.
No example may skip the specific mechanics of Sunk Cost Fallacy.
